# Reports of code's death are greatly exaggerated

Captured on: 2026-03-23
HN context: front-page story on Hacker News on 2026-03-23
Source URL: https://stevekrouse.com/precision

Raw text:

Steve Krouse argues that AI helps turn English into running code quickly, which makes vibe coding feel precise for a while, but the feeling breaks once complexity leaks through edge cases and scale. He says the answer is not to abandon code but to value abstraction more. Code is presented as a precision artifact for mastering complexity, not just for producing software behavior.

The essay pushes back on the idea that coding is dead. The claim is that stronger AI should increase the value of better abstractions, because people will use stronger models on harder abstraction problems rather than only using them to ship more low-quality software.

# Reports of code's death are greatly exaggerated (Steve Krouse)

- **Source:** [/01_capture/influential/2026-03-23__0000__hn-reports-of-codes-death.md](/01_capture/influential/2026-03-23__0000__hn-reports-of-codes-death.md)
- **Date:** 2026-03-23
- **People:** Steve Krouse
- **Topics:** abstraction, vibe-coding, ai-engineering, software-complexity

## Key Points
- Vibe coding feels precise early on; the illusion breaks at edge cases and scale.
- Code's value is as a precision artifact for mastering complexity — not merely producing behavior.
- Stronger AI raises the value of better abstractions, not just more output.

## Why this matters for current work
- Pushes back on "just prompt it" as a terminal strategy; abstraction skill compounds as models improve.

<!-- AGENT_EDITABLE_START:reflection -->
- Pairs well with the OpenAI harness-engineering card: both argue the bottleneck moves up the stack (to review, to abstraction) rather than disappearing.
- Vibe coding is a fast prototype lane, not a scaling strategy — a useful framing for deciding when to harden a solution.
<!-- AGENT_EDITABLE_END:reflection -->
